title: Geometric module stalk on a space as tensor extension of an ordinary chart stalk
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $M$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module on its small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Let $e:U\to X$ be an etale morphism from a scheme and let $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ be a geometric point, where $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, with image $u\in U$; put $\bar x=e\bar u$. Let $M_U$ be the quasi-coherent Zariski module corresponding to the restriction $e^*M$ under [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Write $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and $M_{\bar x}$ for the geometric stalks, namely the colimits of regular functions and module sections over pointed etale scheme neighbourhoods of $\bar x$. The ordinary local ring $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ acts on $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ by the natural germ homomorphism of [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness]. There is a canonical $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$-linear isomorphism $$ (M_U)_u\otimes_{\mathcal O_{U,u}}\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ M_{\bar x}. $$ Here $(M_U)_u$ is the ordinary Zariski module stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and $\otimes$ is the module tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; the map sends a tensor of a module germ with a ring germ to their product after restriction to a common pointed neighbourhood. No finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05VP (lemma-stalk-quasi-coherent), with the chart ring map of Tag 04KF (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring).

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{U,u}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $B_U=\mathcal O_{U,\bar u}$, and $G=e^*M$. Etale pullback is restriction on localized sites [def-trf-algebraic-space], so $G=M|_U$ and $e^{-1}\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_U$. Let $\Phi=L_{\bar u}$ send $W\in U_{\mathrm{et}}$ to the set of lifts of $\bar u$ to $W$; its category of elements is the cofiltered category of pointed etale neighbourhoods [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered], and an etale covering of $W$ lifts any point of $\Phi(W)$ to a member [lem-sfb-etale-geometric-point-specified-lift], so $\Phi$ is a point and $\Phi^*$ is the geometric stalk at $\bar u$. Apply [lem-cbc-site-point-comap-germ] to the base-change functor $V\mapsto V\times_XU$ from $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ (it preserves finite limits and coverings, and $V\times_XU$ is a scheme [def-trf-algebraic-space]) with left adjoint $e^{-1}$. Lifts of $\bar u$ to $V\times_XU$ are the lifts of $\bar x$ to $V$, so $(\Phi_F)^*$ is the geometric stalk at $\bar x$, and the lemma gives a natural bijection $b:F_{\bar x}\cong(e^{-1}F)_{\bar u}$ sending the germ of $m$ at $(V,\bar v)$ to the germ of $\mathrm{pr}_V^*m$ at $(V\times_XU,(\bar v,\bar u))$. For $W\in U_{\mathrm{et}}$ the graph $W\to W\times_XU$ is a map of pointed neighbourhoods, so $b$ sends the germ at $(W\to X,\bar w)$ of $m\in M(W)$ to its germ at $(W,\bar w)$. For $F=\mathcal O_X$ this is the restriction map $\rho:B\to B_U$, the canonical isomorphism of [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness]. Naturality on the action maps $\mathcal O_X\times M\to M$ makes $\tau=b^{-1}:G_{\bar u}\to M_{\bar x}$ a $\rho$-semilinear bijection, i.e. a $B$-linear isomorphism when $G_{\bar u}$ is a $B$-module through $\rho$.

By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], $G$ is identified with $\epsilon_U^*M_U$, $\epsilon_U:U_{\mathrm{et}}\to U_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ the canonical morphism of ringed sites, by the counit $r\otimes s\mapsto rs$, and $M_U(W)=G(W)$ for Zariski opens $W$. By [lem-sfb-space-geometric-points-conservative] the geometric stalk at $\bar u$ is the inverse image of a point $p_{\bar u}$ of $\operatorname{Sh}(U_{\mathrm{et}})$; put $q=\epsilon_U\circ p_{\bar u}$. Apply [lem-cbc-site-point-comap-germ] to the inclusion of Zariski opens into $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ (it preserves intersections, $U$ and open covers) and the point $\Phi$ of step 1: $\Phi(W)$ is one point if $u\in W$ and empty otherwise, so $(\Phi_F)^*H=\varinjlim_{W\ni u}H(W)=H_u$ is the ordinary stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and $H_u\cong(\epsilon_U^{-1}H)_{\bar u}=q^{-1}H$ sends $s_u$ to the germ of the inverse-image section of $s$ on $(W,\bar u)$. With this identification of $q$-stalks, [lem-sfb-ringed-topos-pullback-stalk] for $\epsilon_U$ and $p_{\bar u}$ gives a $B_U$-linear isomorphism $(\epsilon_U^*M_U)_{\bar u}\cong(M_U)_u\otimes_AB_U$ sending the germ of a local pure tensor $r\otimes s$ to $s_u\otimes r_{\bar u}$; the ring map $A\to B_U$ is the stalk of $\epsilon_U^\sharp$, i.e. the germ map $f_u\mapsto f_{\bar u}$. It is the germ map of the statement after $\rho^{-1}$ (step 1).

source.place: Tag 05VP; descent.tex Tags 03FH and 03DX; sites.tex Tag 05V1 (lemma-point-morphism-sites); sites-modules.tex Tag 05V5 (lemma-pullback-stalk)

proof.text: Let $\psi:(M_U)_u\otimes_AB_U\to G_{\bar u}$ be the inverse of the isomorphism of step 2 followed by the counit of step 2; it sends $s_u\otimes r_{\bar u}$ to the germ of $r\,s$ at $\bar u$, with $s\in M_U(W)=G(W)$ and $r$ a function on a pointed neighbourhood over $W$. Compose with $\tau$ of step 1 and transport the second factor along $\rho^{-1}:B_U\cong B$. The resulting $B$-linear isomorphism $(M_U)_u\otimes_AB\cong M_{\bar x}$ sends $s_u\otimes b$ to the germ at $\bar x$ of the product of $s$ and a representative of $b$ on a common pointed neighbourhood: ordinary germs have section representatives [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], ring geometric germs have representatives by the colimit definition, and every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so this is the map asserted in the item on every element. No finiteness condition entered the argument.
